summary: ```# Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial Video ## Making a Knotted Triangle Scarf p03: Tightening the Knot Position ### Introduction In this section, we will focus on tightening the knot position on the knotted triangle scarf using Marvelous Designer. This process involves using a fixed needle to create a compression effect on the scarf part of the cut-off plate. ### Using a Fixed Needle To imitate the effect of compression, we need to use a fixed needle. The fixed needle follows the grid point, and in Marvelous Designer, once the point of the cut-off plate is modified, the sewing line or the change in particle diameter will cause the fixed needle to be re-stripped. This means it will return to the state when there was no added fixed needle. ### Modifying the Grid Before adding the fixed needle, we need to modify the content that affects the grid. For example, we should delete the inner line that cannot be used. However, when deleting the inner line, the grid may change too much, and the cut-off plate will not be fixed. ### Reducing Particle Diameter To ensure stability, we can reduce the particle diameter first. After reducing it, we will remove the fixed needle and re-strip it, ensuring that the grid is not affected too much. Next, we will remove the inner line and modify it accordingly. ### Fixed Points and Sewing Lines The two sides of the scarf act as fixed points. In this scenario, the fixed needle on the cut-off plate will not move. We must also delete the sewing line, as it will affect the line of the net. After deleting, we will simulate again. ### Adjusting the Cut-Off Plate Then, we will continue to reduce the slope of the cut-off plate to 80, making the cut-off a little tighter. Now that the particle diameter of the cut-off plate has been reduced, we should also reduce the slope of the cut-off plate to create more grid surface and prevent protrusion. ### Freezing the Cut-Off Plate Once adjustments have been made, we can freeze the cut-off plate, after which we will not modify it further. Next, we will increase the slope of the cut-off plate to 45 and reduce the particle diameter to 5 to prevent instability. ### Simulating for Stability We will simulate to check for any instability. If the slope is increased to 60, we may find that the cut-off plate has started to become unstable. In this case, the best solution is to simulate the plate of the cut-off element together. We should return to the state before the simulation, cut-off, and then simulate together. ### Continuing Adjustments After the simulation stabilizes, we will freeze the outer plate and refrain from cutting off. We will gradually increase the slope according to increments of 5, from 60 to 70. After each modification, we must stabilize the simulation for more than 5 seconds before proceeding. ### Managing Fixed Needles When adjusting the slope, it's important to remember that if fixed needles on both ends are deleted, their own gravity will pull the knot down, causing instability. If the rate is increased to 75 and instability arises, we can revert to 70 and add a fixed needle to the squeezed part. ### Adding Stabilizers This time, we will add a fixed needle to the part that is below the front view. Since the fixed needle only selects the visible part from the front view, we can select a portion of the frame to increase the density. We will then add a stabilizer and increase its position compared to the 2D window. ### Positioning Stabilizers We can choose the middle part first and then select a larger area, gradually adding the stabilizer. It’s important to rotate at different angles to ensure visibility of the stabilizer from every angle. If it's not visible, we will continue to increase the stabilizer. ### Fine-Tuning Stabilizer Application If uncertain about the position, we can directly select a larger area in the 2D window frame and compare it to the 3D window. It’s advisable not to add a large piece of stabilizer at once, as this may result in a stiff simulation. Instead, we will add the stabilizer gradually, ensuring there is about 1cm of stabilizer near the node. ### Final Adjustments After adding the stabilizer, we will prepare to adjust the shrinkage. Now the node will not be affected anymore. We will delete the stabilizer on both sides and simulate again, gradually increasing the shrinkage to 90. ### Monitoring Stabilizer Behavior During this process, we must simulate continually. When the shrinkage reaches 90, the stabilizer will be very slow. We should be cautious not to overheat the stabilizer. If the shrinkage is not sufficient, we can add more stabilizer on top for increased flexibility. ### Final Simulation and Adjustments Finally, we will check the stabilizer's indication using the command to exhaust it. After deleting the fixed pin of the outer ring, we will start the simulation. Then, we will freeze the small piece of the board and delete the other side before starting another simulation. ### Conclusion In conclusion, the production of all the board triangles is completed. It takes a lot of patience to do the simulation effectively. We encourage you to practice more to master these techniques. See you in the next video. Bye bye! ```
